The apply_template result gives two possible outcomes (tuples). The first product: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C)C[C@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)[C@H]1C)CO" which is similar but the ester O is silylated? Actually O[Si] attached to the carboxylate O. The second product: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C" which is silylation of the primary alcohol side chain.

Our precursor list had three entries: first same as target (no change) + silyl chloride; second with OSi moved; third with ester OSi. The apply_template gave two products: one with ester OSi, one with side chain OSi. The first product matches third precursor (ester OSi). The second matches second precursor (side chain OSi). The first precursor (same as target) is maybe the case where template not applied (i.e., no change). So template 145718 indeed generates the needed precursors.

Thus we can answer with mapped_rxn from template 145718 (as retrieved) and template_id 145718.

The mapped_rxn string from get_template is:

'[CH3:1][CH2:2][CH2:3][CH2:4][CH2:5][CH2:6][CH2:7][CH2:8][C:9]1([O:10][Si](C)(C)C)[CH:11]=[C:12]([S:13][CH3:14])[C:15](=[O:16])[CH:17]1[CH:18]([OH:19])[CH2:20][CH2:21][CH2:22][CH2:23][CH2:24][C:25](=[O:26])[O:27][CH3:28].C1=CC=NC=C1.C1=CC=NC=C1.F.O=C([O-])O.[Na+].CC#N>>[CH3:1][CH2:2][CH2:3][CH2:4][CH2:5][CH2:6][CH2:7][CH2:8][C:9]1([OH:10])[CH:11]=[C:12]([S:13][CH3:14])[C:15](=[O:16])[CH:17]1[CH:18]([OH:19])[CH2:20][CH2:21][CH2:22][CH2:23][CH2:24][C:25](=[O:26])[O:27][CH3:28]'

We should return that.

Check format: JSON dict with mapped_rxn string and template_id integer.
